correctness.rationale: For the stated fixed dimension and stationary normalized product measure, both inverse branches have weight 1/2. Applying them to the centered coordinates gives the invariant affine span and matrix B. Mixing implies B^n→0 since the coordinate Gram matrix is invertible, and the displayed H satisfies (I−B)H=B (interior rows reduce to successive differences, with the two end rows giving the asymmetric coefficients). As a direct check on the joint limit, the Poisson increment on the left inverse branch at y is ((y₁−1)/2, u₂(y)+(y₁+1)/4, …, u_M(y)+(y₁+1)/4); on the right it is its negative because Pd=0. Product Lebesgue second moments give 1/3, −1/12, 1/6 and 1/12 for the four covariance-entry classes, respectively. Ergodicity gives the averaged conditional variances for the bounded reverse-martingale CLT, applied to every linear projection; the bounded telescoping corrector does not alter the limiting covariance or distribution. The passive correlations are for distinct indices, with no such pair at M=2. The two-dimensional block has trace M+4 and determinant 3M+1 in units of 1/12, giving the eigenvalues and the fixed-order versus large-M limits as claimed. Read the frozen exact-arithmetic verify.py and its recorded replay instructions; the finite range was not rerun and does not establish the all-M argument.

value.rationale: The exact matrix quantifies the anisotropic spatial fluctuations of a concrete map despite its deterministic ordering of passive coordinates. A common diffusive passive mode and a negative coupling to the active coordinate cannot be inferred from scalar variance or mixing. The joint invariant is useful without claiming a new martingale theorem or a growing-dimension CLT.
